analysis.title: UBS House View Monthly Letter: Sustaining resilience
key_insights: UBS CIO downgraded global equities from Attractive to Neutral. It sees the most favorable risk-reward in bonds and commodities, then equities, with cash least preferred.

US, Asia ex-Japan, Japanese and emerging market equities were downgraded from Attractive to Neutral. UBS argues the changing AI trade and rising macro risks may lead markets to apply a lower multiple to future earnings.

Base case for global AI-related investment: USD 1.0 trillion in 2026, USD 1.4 trillion in 2027, USD 1.5 trillion in 2028. Major cloud providers have reported USD 2.5 trillion of contracted orders not yet recognized as revenue. Since May, token costs have more than halved while usage rose sixfold.

US technology companies will likely have invested nearly USD 5 trillion cumulatively in AI infrastructure by end-2028. UBS estimates 2026 AI model and application revenue at USD 150-200 billion and says at least USD 1.5 trillion by 2030 is needed for an adequate return.

Competitive intensity in tech is rising. Q3 revenue growth slowed for large model developers, partly due to price cuts. Alphabet's Q3 search revenue missed expectations as users rely on AI search results, which cost more to provide and are harder to monetize.

Financing is getting harder. Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and SpaceX account for about 80% of forecast 2027 AI investment. The WSJ reported OpenAI's recent funding round raised less than half of its USD 30 billion target.

The scale of Democratic gains in the midterms raises the risk of some slowdown in data center development. UBS does not expect the result to derail the AI investment cycle. The recent departure of NVIDIA's CEO may draw attention to concentration risk, and with new listings could add near-term volatility.
S&P 500 target P/E multiple cut from 20x to 18.5x. 2027 S&P 500 EPS growth forecast is about 15%. The December 2027 S&P 500 forecast is 8,200, about 10% upside. The top 10 firms are 39% of the index.

Eurozone is the preferred equity region. UBS forecasts 2027 earnings growth of 15%, similar to the S&P 500 but from a lower valuation, driven by manufacturing, defense, infrastructure and electrification. The region has less direct exposure to US AI expectations.

Sector preference is industrials and health care. In industrials, UBS prefers companies serving multiple end-markets over those dependent on data center construction. Since the start of June, the equal-weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the cap-weighted index by about 7 percentage points.

UBS expects the Fed to raise rates 25 bp in December 2026 and again in March 2027, and the ECB to raise 25 bp in December and March. It expects the BoE to hike 25 bp in February and the SNB to move to 0.25% in March and 0.5% in June.
UBS does not expect a prolonged hiking cycle. It forecasts 2027 average inflation of 2.3% in the US, 3.1% in the Eurozone and 3.4% globally, against 3.4%, 3.1% and 3.8% in 2026.

UBS recommends rebalancing into fixed income with an intermediate duration of about 2-10 years. For one year of income to be offset by capital losses, 2-, 5- and 10-year US Treasury yields would need to rise about 255, 113 and 65 bp.

UBS sees the best fixed income returns in EM and high yield bonds. EM sovereign yields about 7.1%, EM corporate about 7.0% and US HY about 8.3%. About 60% of US HY is rated BB, UBS expects defaults near 2%, and only about 3% of the market matures within a year.

Gold was upgraded to Attractive. It hit nearly USD 5,600/oz early in 2026 and has since fallen below USD 4,000. UBS says near-term headwinds from high real yields and a firm dollar may hold it below USD 4,000, and forecasts USD 5,000 in December 2027.

UBS forecasts Brent at USD 90 in June 2027 and USD 80 in December 2027, after Brent reached about USD 92, 30% above pre-conflict levels, due to the US-Iran war. The CMCI Commodity Total Return Index gained about 25% in 2026. Copper is the preferred industrial metal.

After the midterms Democrats control both chambers. UBS expects gridlock and headline volatility rather than a derailing of markets. It expects the effective US tariff rate in a 10-15% range and fiscal deficits above 6% of GDP. It expects an eventual wind-down of the Iran conflict, but an imminent settlement is unlikely.

Neutral on the US dollar. The pound is the preferred G10 carry currency, with Bank Rate at 4%. UBS expects positive total returns from EM currencies (MXN, ZAR, BRL, INR). The Swiss franc is a funding currency candidate.

Alternatives preferences: hedge fund strategies that exploit dispersion, operationally focused private equity and secondaries, and core and core-plus infrastructure. Compute-backed loans carry technology, utilization and residual-value risks.

sector_views.rationale: Automation, defense, transport infrastructure and electrification investment support earnings as manufacturing expands. UBS prefers companies serving multiple end-markets over data center-dependent ones.
New therapies, obesity treatments, diagnostics and medical technology are expected to support revenue.
UBS urges diversifying away from concentrated tech exposure because of AI monetization, competition and financing risks.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of about 15% in 2027.
UBS forecasts Eurozone earnings growth of 15% in 2027, after 20% in 2026 and with 8% in 2028 (CIO estimates).
UBS forecasts earnings growth of about 20% in 2027 for Asia ex-Japan and emerging markets.
Alphabet's Q3 search revenue fell short of expectations, partly because users rely on AI search results that cost more to provide and are harder to monetize.

macro_indicators.reading: +25 bp in December 2026 and +25 bp in March 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS sees the risk of consecutive hikes given recent inflation, but not a prolonged cycle.

macro_indicators.reading: +25 bp in December and +25 bp in March, then a pause

macro_indicators.interpretation: One-off price pressures fade and underlying inflation eases.
Moderating inflation lets yields decline modestly later in 2027.
Spending cuts are delayed and debt-service costs rise, which supports geographic and currency diversification.
Trade policy brings headline volatility without lifting the tariff rate sustainably beyond this range.
Supported by sound fundamentals and a light maturity schedule.

trade_ideas.description: Rebalance into fixed income, with intermediate duration of about 2-10 years, emphasizing quality, EM and high yield bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Elevated starting yields give attractive income and a cushion if yields rise, and quality bonds would rally if equity risks intensify.
trade_ideas.risk: Sticky inflation, elevated government debt and geopolitical risks could push yields higher.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold, upgraded to Attractive, targeting USD 5,000/oz in December 2027
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural demand should support gold around USD 4,000 and easing real yields should help it regain momentum in 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: High US real yields and a firm dollar could keep gold below USD 4,000 in the short term.

trade_ideas.description: Add copper exposure during periods of weakness as part of a broader commodity allocation
trade_ideas.rationale: Electrification, power networks, data centers and AI infrastructure support demand while long mine-development times constrain supply.

trade_ideas.description: Long GBP as preferred G10 carry, funded by CHF
trade_ideas.rationale: Resilient UK growth and a further BoE hike preserve sterling's yield advantage, while the Swiss franc's yield disadvantage weighs on its total returns.
trade_ideas.risk: UK fiscal credibility, and renewed geopolitical stress or a global slowdown reviving defensive demand for the franc.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Eurozone equities and the industrials and health care sectors, and use equal-weight strategies to diversify away from tech
trade_ideas.rationale: Eurozone EPS growth of 15% in 2027 starts from a lower valuation and has broader drivers, and the market has less direct exposure to AI.
trade_ideas.risk: A broader global slowdown would pressure cyclical European equities like other markets.

risk_factors: Sticky inflation, elevated government debt and geopolitical risks could push bond yields higher and equities lower.
Execution and monetization risks could erode confidence that AI demand will translate into shareholder returns.
Index concentration and elevated expectations leave less room for disappointment.
AI financing is becoming harder, especially for companies reliant on external funding, as shown by OpenAI's round raising less than half of its target.
Democratic midterm gains could slow data center development.
Competition from cheaper open-weight models and price cuts is pressuring AI model companies.
Further disruption to Middle Eastern shipping or energy infrastructure could push oil higher.
UK fiscal credibility is a key risk to sterling.
Compute-backed loans carry technology, utilization and residual-value risks.
charts_described: Figure 2 shows EuroStoxx 12-month trailing EPS with CIO growth estimates of +20% in 2026, +15% in 2027 and +8% in 2028.
Figure 3 plots US headline CPI in % y/y with UBS estimates through 2028, marking the start of the Iran, Ukraine and COVID-19 supply shock periods.
vol_and_positioning: The top 10 S&P 500 firms, mostly AI-exposed, are 39% of the index. The top five companies in Asia ex-Japan and EM are about one-third of those indices.
The recent departure of NVIDIA's CEO, together with new listings, could add to near-term volatility.
Since June the equal-weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the cap-weighted index by about 7 percentage points. UBS suggests equal-weight strategies to diversify tech exposure.
Relatively contained FX volatility favors diversified EM currency carry.
geopolitical: US-Iran war and Middle East disruption raised energy prices and bond yields in 2026. UBS says an eventual wind-down is more plausible but an imminent settlement is unlikely.
The war in Ukraine is likely to extend into 2027. A durable ceasefire could support European assets.
Continued limits on Russian oil supply and disruption to Middle Eastern shipping or energy infrastructure could push oil prices higher.
US midterms gave Democrats both chambers, so UBS expects confrontational divided government with possible compromise on funding and debt limit deadlines.
Trade policy is expected to bring headline volatility with the effective US tariff rate staying in a 10-15% range.
State and local constraints on data centers (land, water, electricity, grid, tax) may matter more for AI than federal legislation.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment is forecast to rise from USD 1.0 trillion to USD 1.4 trillion in 2027. Demand is robust, capacity is constrained, cloud revenue growth is accelerating, and USD 2.5 trillion of contracted orders are still to be recognized.
tension_points.bear_case: Nearly USD 5 trillion of cumulative US tech AI investment by end-2028 needs at least USD 1.5 trillion of annual revenue by 2030 against USD 150-200 billion in 2026. Model developers' growth slowed on price cuts, Alphabet's search revenue missed, and OpenAI's funding round fell short.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that AI models and applications are not delivering enough value to earn an attractive return on spending, such as continued revenue growth slowdowns, or funding shortfalls.

tension_points.theme: US equities vs rate and inflation risk
tension_points.bull_case: S&P 500 EPS growth of about 15% in 2027 and a December 2027 forecast of 8,200, about 10% upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Stickier inflation, higher Fed rates and higher bond yields could lower the multiple below the 18.5x target.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further Fed hikes beyond the expected December and March moves, or sticky inflation pushing yields higher.

theme_stances.key_argument: Revenues of at least USD 1.5 trillion by 2030 are needed for an adequate return on AI spending, so not every company may reap rewards.
theme_stances.evidence: not every company may reap the rewards

theme_stances.evidence: Regionally, the Eurozone is our preferred equity market.

theme_stances.evidence: We do not expect a prolonged rate-hike cycle.
